questions.question: A company needs to ingest streaming data from IoT devices at a rate of 10,000 records per second. The data must be processed in real-time and stored in S3 for batch analytics. Which combination of services provides the most cost-effective solution?
options: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with Lambda functions for processing and Kinesis Data Firehose for S3 delivery
Amazon SQS with EC2 instances for processing and direct S3 uploads
Amazon MSK with EMR for processing and S3 as the final destination
Direct API Gateway integration with Lambda and S3
questions.explanation: Kinesis Data Streams can handle high-throughput streaming data (10,000 records/sec), Lambda provides serverless real-time processing, and Kinesis Data Firehose offers automatic S3 delivery with built-in buffering and compression, making this the most cost-effective solution for the requirements.

questions.question: A data lake administrator needs to implement column-level security for a table containing customer PII data. Users in the marketing team should only see customer_id and purchase_amount columns, while the finance team should see all columns. What is the most efficient approach using AWS Lake Formation?
options: Create separate tables for each team with different column sets
Use Lake Formation column-level permissions with different grants for each team
Implement row-level security with conditional column access
Use IAM policies to control S3 object access at the file level
questions.explanation: Lake Formation supports fine-grained column-level permissions that allow administrators to grant SELECT permissions on specific columns to different principals, providing the most efficient and secure approach for this requirement.

questions.question: Which AWS service is best suited for running Apache Spark jobs to process large datasets stored in S3 without managing infrastructure?
options: AWS Glue
Amazon EMR
AWS Batch
AWS Lambda
questions.explanation: AWS Glue is a fully managed ETL service that runs Apache Spark jobs without requiring infrastructure management, making it ideal for processing large datasets in S3 with minimal operational overhead.

questions.question: A company stores 100TB of log data in S3 with the following access patterns: frequently accessed for 30 days, occasionally accessed for 90 days, and rarely accessed afterward. What S3 storage configuration minimizes costs?
options: Standard storage class with lifecycle policy to Glacier after 30 days
Intelligent Tiering for automatic optimization
Standard for 30 days, Standard-IA for 60 days, then Glacier Flexible Retrieval
One Zone-IA for all data with lifecycle policy to Deep Archive
questions.explanation: This configuration aligns storage classes with access patterns: Standard for frequent access (30 days), Standard-IA for occasional access (60 days), then Glacier Flexible Retrieval for rare access, providing optimal cost savings.

questions.question: A business analyst needs to create interactive dashboards from data stored in both Redshift and S3. The dashboards must support drill-down capabilities and be accessible to 500+ users. Which solution provides the best performance and scalability?
options: Amazon QuickSight with SPICE datasets and direct query mode
Tableau Server hosted on EC2 with direct database connections
Amazon QuickSight with direct query mode only
Custom web application using D3.js with API Gateway and Lambda
questions.explanation: QuickSight with SPICE (Super-fast, Parallel, In-memory Calculation Engine) provides excellent performance for interactive dashboards, supports 500+ users, and can connect to both Redshift and S3 data sources with drill-down capabilities.

questions.question: A financial services company needs to replicate transaction data from an on-premises Oracle database to AWS for real-time fraud detection. The solution must handle schema changes and provide exactly-once delivery. Which approach is most suitable?
options: AWS Database Migration Service with ongoing replication to Kinesis Data Streams
Custom ETL jobs using AWS Glue with scheduled runs every 5 minutes
Oracle GoldenGate with Kinesis Data Firehose integration
AWS DataSync for periodic data synchronization
questions.explanation: AWS DMS supports ongoing replication from Oracle with change data capture (CDC), handles schema changes automatically, and can deliver to Kinesis Data Streams for real-time processing with exactly-once delivery guarantees.

questions.question: A data engineer needs to process streaming data with 5-minute tumbling windows to calculate average values. The processing must handle late-arriving data up to 10 minutes. Which service and configuration is most appropriate?
options: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink with watermarks and allowed lateness
AWS Lambda with CloudWatch Events scheduled every 5 minutes
Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics for SQL with tumbling windows
AWS Glue with job bookmarks and micro-batch processing
questions.explanation: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink provides advanced windowing capabilities with watermarks for handling late data and allowed lateness configuration, making it ideal for complex stream processing requirements.

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of partitioning data in S3 for analytics workloads?
options: Improved data compression ratios
Reduced query costs and improved performance by scanning only relevant partitions
Automatic data encryption
Enhanced data durability
questions.explanation: Partitioning allows query engines like Athena and Redshift Spectrum to scan only relevant partitions, significantly reducing the amount of data processed and improving query performance while lowering costs.

questions.question: A company wants to ensure that all data in their data lake is encrypted at rest and in transit. Which combination of AWS services and configurations achieves this requirement?
options: S3 with SSE-S3, HTTPS endpoints, and VPC endpoints for service communication
S3 with client-side encryption only
EBS encryption for EMR clusters and S3 default encryption
AWS KMS for key management with S3 SSE-KMS and TLS 1.2 for all connections
questions.explanation: AWS KMS with S3 SSE-KMS provides robust encryption at rest with centralized key management, while TLS 1.2 ensures encryption in transit for all data communications, meeting comprehensive security requirements.

questions.question: A data scientist needs to perform complex analytical queries on 50TB of historical data stored in S3, with query response times under 10 seconds. The data is accessed infrequently but requires high performance when queried. What is the most cost-effective solution?
options: Load all data into Amazon Redshift with RA3 instances
Use Amazon Athena with columnar format (Parquet) and appropriate partitioning
Create an EMR cluster with Presto for ad-hoc queries
Use Amazon Redshift Spectrum with data in S3
questions.explanation: Amazon Athena with Parquet format and proper partitioning provides excellent query performance for infrequently accessed data, with pay-per-query pricing making it most cost-effective for this use case.

questions.question: Which AWS service is specifically designed to capture and load streaming data into AWS data stores with minimal configuration?
options: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose
Amazon MSK
AWS Data Pipeline
questions.explanation: Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose is specifically designed as a fully managed service to capture, transform, and load streaming data into AWS data stores like S3, Redshift, and OpenSearch with minimal configuration required.

questions.question: A company processes IoT sensor data using EMR Spark Streaming with checkpointing enabled. After a cluster failure, the application needs to resume processing from the last checkpoint. What configuration ensures reliable recovery?
options: Store checkpoints in HDFS on the EMR cluster
Store checkpoints in S3 with versioning enabled
Use DynamoDB for checkpoint storage
Store checkpoints in local EBS volumes
questions.explanation: Storing checkpoints in S3 with versioning provides durability and availability across cluster failures, allowing Spark Streaming applications to reliably resume processing from the last successful checkpoint.

questions.question: A data lake contains both structured and semi-structured data. The AWS Glue crawler is not correctly inferring the schema for JSON files with nested structures. What is the best approach to resolve this?
options: Increase the crawler's sample size configuration
Create custom classifiers to properly identify and parse the JSON structure
Convert JSON files to Parquet format before crawling
Manually create table schemas in the Glue Data Catalog
questions.explanation: Custom classifiers in AWS Glue allow you to define specific patterns and parsing rules for complex data formats like nested JSON, ensuring accurate schema inference for semi-structured data.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides centralized governance and fine-grained access control for data lakes?
options: AWS IAM
AWS Lake Formation
Amazon S3 Bucket Policies
AWS Config
questions.explanation: AWS Lake Formation provides centralized governance and fine-grained access control for data lakes, including table, column, and row-level permissions that integrate with various AWS analytics services.

questions.question: A company wants to provide self-service analytics capabilities to business users who are not familiar with SQL. The solution should connect to multiple data sources and provide drag-and-drop functionality. Which AWS service best meets these requirements?
options: Amazon Athena with a web-based query editor
Amazon QuickSight with its visual interface
Amazon Redshift with SQL Workbench
AWS Glue DataBrew for data preparation
questions.explanation: Amazon QuickSight provides a visual, drag-and-drop interface for creating analyses and dashboards, making it ideal for business users without SQL knowledge while supporting multiple data source connections.

questions.question: A company needs to migrate 500GB of data daily from multiple SaaS applications to S3. The data transfer should be automated and support various SaaS connectors. Which service is most appropriate?
options: AWS DataSync
Amazon AppFlow
AWS Database Migration Service
AWS Transfer Family
questions.explanation: Amazon AppFlow is specifically designed for automated data transfer from SaaS applications to AWS services, providing pre-built connectors for popular SaaS platforms and supporting scheduled data flows.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides a visual interface for creating ETL jobs without writing code?
options: AWS Glue Studio
Amazon EMR Notebooks
AWS Step Functions
Amazon SageMaker
questions.explanation: AWS Glue Studio provides a visual interface for creating, running, and monitoring ETL jobs without requiring code, making it accessible to users who prefer graphical development environments.

questions.question: A company stores time-series data in S3 with the following structure: /year/month/day/hour/. Queries typically filter by date ranges and specific metrics. The current Parquet files are 2GB each. What optimization would most improve query performance?
options: Reduce file size to 128MB and add metric-based partitioning
Increase file size to 10GB to reduce metadata overhead
Convert to ORC format with ZLIB compression
Implement columnar partitioning within each file
questions.explanation: Optimal file sizes for analytics workloads are typically 128MB-1GB. Adding metric-based partitioning along with temporal partitioning allows query engines to skip irrelevant data, significantly improving performance.

questions.question: A data analyst needs access to customer data for reporting but should not see personally identifiable information (PII). The data is stored in a Glue Data Catalog table. What Lake Formation feature addresses this requirement?
options: Row-level security with conditional filters
Column-level permissions to exclude PII columns
Data masking and filtering
Tag-based access control (LF-TBAC)
questions.explanation: Lake Formation's data masking and filtering feature allows administrators to hide or mask sensitive data like PII while still providing access to other columns, meeting the requirement for selective data access.

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of using Amazon QuickSight's SPICE engine?
options: Reduced storage costs
Faster query performance through in-memory processing
Automatic data backup
Enhanced security features
questions.explanation: SPICE (Super-fast, Parallel, In-memory Calculation Engine) stores data in memory for extremely fast query performance, enabling interactive dashboards and analyses with sub-second response times.

questions.question: A company receives data files from partners via SFTP every hour. The files vary in size from 10MB to 5GB and must be processed within 30 minutes of arrival. Which architecture provides the most reliable and scalable solution?
options: AWS Transfer Family with S3 event notifications triggering Lambda for processing
EC2 instances with SFTP server and cron jobs for file processing
AWS Transfer Family with S3 event notifications triggering Step Functions orchestrating Glue jobs
Amazon MQ with file transfer protocols and SQS for processing queue
questions.explanation: AWS Transfer Family provides managed SFTP, S3 event notifications ensure immediate processing triggers, and Step Functions with Glue jobs can handle variable file sizes reliably with proper error handling and retry logic.

questions.question: A streaming application processes clickstream data and needs to detect user sessions that span multiple hours. The application must handle out-of-order events and session timeouts. Which windowing strategy is most appropriate?
options: Fixed tumbling windows of 1 hour
Sliding windows with 1-hour duration and 15-minute slide
Session windows with 30-minute timeout
Global windows with custom triggers
questions.explanation: Session windows are specifically designed for user session analysis, automatically handling variable session lengths with configurable timeout periods and managing out-of-order events effectively.

questions.question: A data lake contains 10TB of CSV files that need to be converted to Parquet format for better query performance. The conversion should be cost-effective and handle schema evolution. Which approach is recommended?
options: Use AWS Glue ETL jobs with dynamic frames for schema flexibility
Write custom Spark applications on EMR clusters
Use Amazon Athena CTAS queries to convert formats
Implement Lambda functions for file-by-file conversion
questions.explanation: AWS Glue ETL jobs with dynamic frames provide built-in schema evolution handling, cost-effective serverless execution, and optimized Parquet conversion capabilities for large-scale data transformation.

questions.question: A multi-tenant data lake needs to ensure that each tenant can only access their own data. The data is partitioned by tenant_id in S3. What is the most scalable approach using Lake Formation?
options: Create separate databases for each tenant with individual permissions
Use row-level security with tenant_id filters for each user
Implement tag-based access control (LF-TBAC) with tenant tags
Use separate S3 buckets for each tenant with bucket policies
questions.explanation: Tag-based access control (LF-TBAC) in Lake Formation allows scalable multi-tenant access control by tagging resources with tenant identifiers and granting permissions based on matching tags, eliminating the need to manage individual tenant permissions.

questions.question: A company needs to create executive dashboards that combine real-time metrics from Kinesis Data Analytics with historical data from Redshift. The dashboards must update every 5 minutes. What is the best approach?
options: Use QuickSight with direct query to both sources and scheduled refresh
Create a Lambda function to combine data and store results in S3 for QuickSight
Use QuickSight with SPICE datasets and incremental refresh
Implement a custom web application with real-time WebSocket connections
questions.explanation: QuickSight with SPICE datasets and incremental refresh provides the best performance for executive dashboards, efficiently updating only changed data every 5 minutes while maintaining fast query response times.

questions.question: Which Kinesis Data Firehose transformation feature allows you to convert record formats before delivery to the destination?
options: Data format conversion
Dynamic partitioning
Error record handling
Compression algorithms
questions.explanation: Data format conversion in Kinesis Data Firehose allows automatic conversion of incoming data from JSON to columnar formats like Parquet or ORC before delivery to destinations like S3.

questions.question: A Glue ETL job processes 1TB of data daily but frequently runs out of memory. The job uses the default worker type. What is the most cost-effective solution to resolve this issue?
options: Increase the number of workers while keeping the same worker type
Switch to G.2X worker type for more memory per worker
Enable job bookmarks to process data incrementally
Split the job into multiple smaller jobs
questions.explanation: G.2X worker type provides more memory (32GB vs 16GB) per worker, which is more cost-effective than increasing the number of standard workers when memory is the bottleneck.

questions.question: A company stores IoT sensor data in S3 with high write throughput requirements. The data is partitioned by device_id and timestamp. Users report slow query performance when filtering by sensor_type. What partitioning strategy would optimize query performance?
options: Change partitioning to sensor_type/device_id/timestamp
Add sensor_type as a secondary partition after timestamp
Use composite partitioning with sensor_type and device_id combined
Implement bucketing within existing partitions
questions.explanation: Placing sensor_type as the first partition level allows query engines to eliminate entire partitions when filtering by sensor_type, significantly improving query performance for this common access pattern.

questions.question: A data engineer needs to grant a data scientist access to run Athena queries on specific tables in a Lake Formation-managed data lake. What is the minimum set of permissions required?
options: Lake Formation SELECT permission on tables and lakeformation:GetDataAccess IAM permission
Only IAM permissions for Athena and S3 access
Lake Formation database permissions and S3 bucket policies
AWS Glue Data Catalog permissions and Athena workgroup access
questions.explanation: For Lake Formation-managed tables, users need both Lake Formation SELECT permissions on the specific tables and the lakeformation:GetDataAccess IAM permission to access the underlying data through Athena.

questions.question: Which Amazon Redshift feature automatically optimizes query performance by selecting the best sort keys and distribution styles?
options: Automatic table optimization
Workload management (WLM)
Result caching
Concurrency scaling
questions.explanation: Automatic table optimization in Amazon Redshift uses machine learning to automatically apply the best sort keys, distribution styles, and compression encodings based on query patterns and data characteristics.

questions.question: A company needs to replicate data from multiple MySQL databases to a data lake for analytics. The replication must capture schema changes and provide minimal impact on source systems. Which solution is most appropriate?
options: AWS DMS with full load and ongoing replication
Custom scripts using mysqldump and S3 uploads
AWS Glue jobs with JDBC connections
Amazon RDS read replicas with data export
questions.explanation: AWS DMS provides change data capture (CDC) capabilities with minimal impact on source systems, automatically handles schema changes, and can replicate to S3 for data lake ingestion.

questions.question: A real-time fraud detection system processes credit card transactions using Managed Service for Apache Flink. The system needs to maintain state for user spending patterns over the last 24 hours while handling 100,000 transactions per second. What configuration optimizes performance?
options: Use RocksDB state backend with incremental checkpointing
Use memory state backend with frequent checkpointing
Implement custom state management with DynamoDB
Use filesystem state backend with compression
questions.explanation: RocksDB state backend with incremental checkpointing provides the best performance for high-throughput applications with large state, as it stores state on disk while maintaining fast access and efficient checkpointing.

questions.question: A data lake contains both current and historical data. Current data (last 30 days) needs sub-second query response times, while historical data is accessed monthly. What storage and compute strategy optimizes costs and performance?
options: Store all data in Redshift with different node types
Use S3 with current data in Standard class and historical in Glacier, query with Athena
Implement a hybrid approach with current data in Redshift and historical in S3 with Redshift Spectrum
Use EMR with current data in memory and historical data on HDFS
questions.explanation: A hybrid approach with current data in Redshift provides sub-second performance for frequent queries, while Redshift Spectrum allows querying historical data in S3 when needed, optimizing both cost and performance.

questions.question: Which encryption option provides the highest level of control over encryption keys for data stored in S3?
options: SSE-S3 (Server-Side Encryption with S3-Managed Keys)
SSE-KMS (Server-Side Encryption with AWS KMS)
SSE-C (Server-Side Encryption with Customer-Provided Keys)
Client-side encryption
questions.explanation: SSE-C (Server-Side Encryption with Customer-Provided Keys) gives customers complete control over encryption keys, as they provide and manage the keys themselves, offering the highest level of key control.

questions.question: A company wants to enable business users to perform ad-hoc queries on their data lake without managing infrastructure. The solution should support standard SQL and integrate with existing BI tools. Which service best meets these requirements?
options: Amazon EMR with Presto
Amazon Athena
Amazon Redshift Serverless
AWS Glue Interactive Sessions
questions.explanation: Amazon Athena is a serverless query service that supports standard SQL, requires no infrastructure management, and integrates well with BI tools through JDBC/ODBC connections, making it ideal for ad-hoc queries on data lakes.

questions.question: A gaming company collects player event data at variable rates (1,000-50,000 events/second) with strict ordering requirements per player. The solution must handle traffic spikes and maintain event order. What Kinesis configuration is optimal?
options: Single shard with increased retention period
Multiple shards with player_id as partition key
Auto-scaling enabled with random partition keys
Multiple streams with round-robin distribution
questions.explanation: Using player_id as the partition key ensures all events for a specific player go to the same shard, maintaining order per player while allowing multiple shards to handle the variable throughput requirements.

questions.question: Which AWS Glue feature allows you to incrementally process only new or changed data in subsequent job runs?
options: Job bookmarks
Dynamic frames
Crawlers
Triggers
questions.explanation: Job bookmarks in AWS Glue track data that has already been processed, allowing subsequent job runs to process only new or changed data, improving efficiency and reducing processing time.

questions.question: A company needs to implement data retention policies for their data lake. Regulatory requirements mandate that financial data be kept for 7 years, while operational logs can be deleted after 1 year. What is the most automated approach?
options: Use S3 lifecycle policies with different rules based on object prefixes
Implement Lambda functions triggered by CloudWatch Events
Use AWS Config rules to monitor and delete old data
Create scheduled Glue jobs to identify and delete expired data
questions.explanation: S3 lifecycle policies can be configured with different rules based on object prefixes or tags, providing an automated, cost-effective way to manage data retention according to different regulatory requirements.

questions.question: A financial institution needs to implement data masking for sensitive customer data in their analytics environment. The masking should be consistent across different queries but vary by user role. What Lake Formation feature addresses this requirement?
options: Column-level permissions with different grants per role
Row-level security with role-based filters
Data filters with cell-level security and consistent hashing
Tag-based access control with conditional expressions
questions.explanation: Lake Formation's data filters with cell-level security can implement consistent data masking using hashing functions, ensuring the same sensitive data is masked consistently while allowing different masking rules based on user roles.

questions.question: A retail company wants to analyze customer behavior patterns using machine learning on their transaction data stored in Redshift. Which integrated AWS service provides the easiest path to implement ML models?
options: Amazon SageMaker with Redshift data source
Amazon Redshift ML
AWS Glue ML transforms
Amazon Comprehend with Redshift integration
questions.explanation: Amazon Redshift ML allows data analysts to create, train, and deploy ML models using familiar SQL commands directly within Redshift, providing the easiest integration path for ML on Redshift data.

questions.question: A company receives CSV files from partners via email attachments. The files need to be automatically processed and loaded into a data lake. What is the most serverless approach to handle this workflow?
options: SES to receive emails, Lambda to extract attachments, S3 for storage, and Glue for processing
EC2 instances with email clients and scheduled processing jobs
Amazon WorkMail with manual file extraction and upload
API Gateway with file upload endpoints and direct S3 integration
questions.explanation: Amazon SES can receive emails and trigger Lambda functions to extract attachments, store them in S3, and trigger Glue jobs for processing, providing a fully serverless solution for email-based file ingestion.

questions.question: A streaming application needs to join real-time clickstream data with user profile data stored in DynamoDB. The join operation must have low latency and handle 10,000 events per second. Which approach is most suitable?
options: Use Managed Service for Apache Flink with async I/O for DynamoDB lookups
Pre-load all user profiles into Flink state and perform in-memory joins
Use Lambda functions with DynamoDB integration for each event
Batch events and use Glue jobs with DynamoDB connector
questions.explanation: Managed Service for Apache Flink with async I/O allows efficient, low-latency lookups to external systems like DynamoDB while maintaining high throughput for stream processing applications.

questions.question: What is the recommended file format for analytical workloads in Amazon S3 to optimize query performance and reduce costs?
options: CSV with compression
JSON with nested structures
Parquet with columnar compression
Avro with schema evolution
questions.explanation: Parquet is a columnar format that provides excellent compression ratios and query performance for analytical workloads, as query engines can read only the required columns and skip irrelevant data.

questions.question: A company wants to audit all data access in their Lake Formation-managed data lake. Which AWS service provides comprehensive audit logging for data access events?
options: AWS CloudTrail
Amazon CloudWatch Logs
AWS Config
Amazon GuardDuty
questions.explanation: AWS CloudTrail logs all Lake Formation API calls and data access events, providing comprehensive audit trails for compliance and security monitoring of data lake access patterns.

questions.question: A company has a Redshift cluster with mixed workloads: ETL jobs during off-hours and interactive queries during business hours. Query performance degrades when both workloads run simultaneously. What is the best solution to optimize performance?
options: Implement workload management (WLM) with separate query queues
Use Redshift Serverless for interactive queries
Enable concurrency scaling for all query types
Create separate Redshift clusters for each workload
questions.explanation: Workload Management (WLM) allows you to create separate query queues with different resource allocations, ensuring ETL jobs and interactive queries don't compete for the same resources, optimizing performance for both workloads.

questions.question: Which AWS service is best suited for one-time migration of large datasets (multiple terabytes) from on-premises to AWS?
options: AWS DataSync
AWS Snowball
AWS Direct Connect
Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration
questions.explanation: AWS Snowball is designed for large-scale data migration (terabytes to petabytes) when network transfer would be time-consuming or costly, providing a physical device for secure data transport.

questions.question: A company processes sensor data using EMR Spark with the following requirements: handle late-arriving data up to 2 hours, process data in 15-minute windows, and maintain exactly-once processing guarantees. What configuration achieves these requirements?
options: Structured Streaming with watermarks, output mode append, and checkpointing to S3
Spark Streaming with window operations and manual deduplication logic
Batch processing with Spark SQL and manual late data handling
Kafka Streams integration with Spark for exactly-once semantics
questions.explanation: Structured Streaming with watermarks handles late data automatically, append output mode with checkpointing provides exactly-once guarantees, and windowing operations support the 15-minute processing requirement.

questions.question: A data lake stores customer transaction data with the following access patterns: current month data accessed hourly, previous 6 months accessed daily, older data accessed monthly. What S3 storage optimization strategy minimizes costs?
options: Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering for all data
Standard for current month, Standard-IA for 6 months, Glacier Flexible Retrieval for older data
Standard for current month, One Zone-IA for 6 months, Deep Archive for older data
Standard-IA for all data with lifecycle policies
questions.explanation: This tiering strategy aligns storage classes with access patterns: Standard for frequent access, Standard-IA for less frequent access, and Glacier Flexible Retrieval for infrequent access with acceptable retrieval times.

questions.question: A company needs to share specific tables from their Lake Formation data catalog with a partner AWS account while maintaining fine-grained access control. What is the recommended approach?
options: Use cross-account IAM roles with S3 bucket policies
Implement Lake Formation cross-account data sharing with resource links
Copy data to a shared S3 bucket with appropriate permissions
Use AWS PrivateLink for secure cross-account data access
questions.explanation: Lake Formation cross-account data sharing with resource links allows secure sharing of specific tables while maintaining fine-grained access control and centralized governance across AWS accounts.

questions.question: Which Amazon QuickSight feature allows you to create calculated fields and custom metrics without modifying the underlying data source?
options: Data preparation
Calculated fields
Parameters
Custom SQL
questions.explanation: Calculated fields in QuickSight allow users to create new metrics and perform calculations on existing data without modifying the source, providing flexibility for analysis and visualization.

questions.question: A company needs to ingest log files from web servers in real-time. The logs are generated at 5MB per minute per server across 100 servers. The solution must be cost-effective and provide automatic scaling. Which approach is optimal?
options: Kinesis Data Streams with multiple shards
Kinesis Data Firehose with dynamic partitioning
Amazon MSK with auto-scaling enabled
SQS with Lambda functions for processing
questions.explanation: Kinesis Data Firehose is ideal for this use case as it automatically scales, handles the throughput (500MB/min total), and provides cost-effective log ingestion with dynamic partitioning for organized storage.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides a managed Apache Spark environment for big data processing without requiring cluster management?
options: Amazon EMR
AWS Glue
Amazon SageMaker
AWS Batch
questions.explanation: AWS Glue provides a fully managed Apache Spark environment for ETL processing without requiring users to manage clusters, making it ideal for serverless big data processing.

questions.question: A company stores multi-format data (JSON, Parquet, CSV) in S3 with complex nested structures. AWS Glue crawlers are creating multiple tables for the same logical dataset. What is the best approach to create a unified view?
options: Configure crawler to use a single classifier for all formats
Create a Glue Data Catalog view that unions data from multiple tables
Use custom classifiers and schema merge policies
Convert all data to a single format before crawling
questions.explanation: Glue Data Catalog views allow you to create a unified logical view that combines data from multiple tables with different formats, providing a single interface for querying heterogeneous data.

questions.question: A data analyst needs temporary access to sensitive customer data for a specific project. The access should automatically expire after 30 days. What Lake Formation feature supports this requirement?
options: Time-based access policies
Temporary credentials with STS
Lake Formation permissions with expiration dates
IAM roles with temporary policies
questions.explanation: Lake Formation supports permissions with expiration dates, allowing administrators to grant temporary access that automatically expires, ensuring time-limited access to sensitive data.

questions.question: A company wants to provide real-time dashboards showing website traffic patterns. The data comes from CloudFront logs stored in S3 and needs to be updated every minute. What architecture provides the best performance?
options: Athena queries with scheduled Lambda functions updating QuickSight datasets
Kinesis Data Analytics processing CloudFront logs with QuickSight streaming datasets
EMR Spark Streaming with in-memory caching and QuickSight direct query
Redshift with automatic ingestion and QuickSight SPICE refresh
questions.explanation: Kinesis Data Analytics can process CloudFront logs in real-time, and QuickSight streaming datasets can display real-time data with minute-level updates, providing the best performance for real-time dashboards.

questions.question: A financial trading company needs to ingest market data feeds with microsecond latency requirements and guaranteed message ordering. The system must handle 1 million messages per second during peak trading hours. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: Kinesis Data Streams with enhanced fan-out
Amazon MSK with custom partitioning
Custom solution using EC2 with optimized networking
SQS FIFO queues with high throughput mode
questions.explanation: For microsecond latency requirements at this scale, a custom solution using EC2 instances with SR-IOV networking, placement groups, and optimized network configurations is necessary, as managed services cannot meet such stringent latency requirements.

questions.question: A Glue ETL job needs to process data from multiple sources with different schemas and merge them into a single output table. The schemas may evolve over time. What Glue feature handles this requirement?
options: Dynamic frames with schema resolution
Static DataFrames with manual schema mapping
Glue crawlers with automatic schema updates
Custom Python scripts with schema validation
questions.explanation: Dynamic frames in AWS Glue provide built-in schema resolution capabilities that can handle evolving schemas and merge data from multiple sources with different structures automatically.

questions.question: Which S3 storage class is most appropriate for data that is accessed less than once per month but requires immediate retrieval when needed?
options: S3 Standard-IA
S3 One Zone-IA
S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval
S3 Glacier Deep Archive
questions.explanation: S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval is designed for data accessed less than once per month and provides retrieval options from minutes to hours, making it suitable for infrequent access with reasonable retrieval times.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides centralized logging and monitoring for all API calls made to AWS services in a data analytics environment?
options: Amazon CloudWatch
AWS CloudTrail
AWS Config
Amazon GuardDuty
questions.explanation: AWS CloudTrail provides centralized logging of all API calls made to AWS services, including data analytics services, enabling comprehensive audit trails and security monitoring.

questions.question: A company has a Redshift cluster with RA3 nodes and needs to optimize query performance for a mix of complex analytical queries and simple lookups. The data includes both hot and cold datasets. What optimization strategy is most effective?
options: Use automatic workload management with query priorities
Implement materialized views for complex queries and result caching for lookups
Enable concurrency scaling for all query types
Partition tables by access frequency and use different distribution keys
questions.explanation: Materialized views pre-compute complex analytical queries, while result caching speeds up repetitive simple lookups. This combination optimizes performance for both query types without unnecessary resource consumption.

questions.question: A company receives data files via FTP from multiple partners with varying file sizes (1KB to 10GB) and frequencies (every minute to daily). What ingestion architecture handles this variability efficiently?
options: AWS Transfer Family with S3 event notifications triggering different processing paths based on file size
EC2 instances with FTP servers and uniform processing for all files
Lambda functions for direct FTP polling and processing
Amazon MQ with file transfer protocols
questions.explanation: AWS Transfer Family provides managed FTP services, and S3 event notifications can trigger different processing workflows based on file attributes, efficiently handling the variability in file sizes and frequencies.
